subject: Results: Data audit and integrity checks after 2026-07-07 datastore incident
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <security@fintegrity.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Observed anomalous outbound connections 07/07 — request for confirmation

Hi Irene,

We saw anomalous outbound connections from your service to an unfamiliar IP range during our monitoring window on 2026-07-07 (roughly 02:45–03:15 UTC). Our tooling flagged unusual egress rates for our org. Can you confirm whether any customer data (PII, raw logs, embeddings) may have been transmitted outside of your expected endpoints? Fintegrity needs an initial technical assessment and a list of the systems you will check.

We appreciate a quick reply — even an initial summary will help our compliance team.

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Head of Security Operations
Fintegrity Software
security@fintegrity.io

---

(Attachment: alert-screenshot-FT8892.png)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <security@fintegrity.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous outbound connections 07/07 — request for confirmation

Alex — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the concern. We've started an immediate integrity sweep. High level:
- Scope: all egress paths from our inference fleet for 2026-07-07 00:00–06:00 UTC (application logs, S3/event logs, NAT gateway logs, and model-serving telemetry).
- Initial action: isolate affected nodes, preserve disk images, and run read-only queries against access logs.
- Timeline: preliminary findings by EOD Thu (2026-07-09); full artifacts and query results by Mon (2026-07-12).

We will provide the queries and attachments used in the audit for reproducibility. At this stage we are not making legal representations, but we will summarize technical findings and any evidence that could indicate exfiltration.

Attached: integrity-check-plan.pdf (audit checklist and queries).

I'll loop in Monica (ops) for the raw log pulls.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

(Attachment: integrity-check-plan.pdf)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <security@fintegrity.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 18:24:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous outbound connections 07/07 — preliminary log search results

Hi Alex — quick update from the log team. We ran the following read-only queries (see attached):
- NAT egress histogram by destination IP and bytes (svc-nginx, inference pool)
- S3 PutObject/CompleteMultipartUpload events originating from inference instances
- KV-store (redis) large value read patterns and unusual GET/SCAN activity

Preliminary results (short):
- NAT metrics: three short spikes between 02:39–02:52 UTC tied to automated health-checks hitting a misconfigured upstream probe; byte counts are under 1.2MB per spike per instance.
- S3: zero PutObject events from inference hosts in the timeframe.
- KV-store: no abnormal large-value reads or scans; access patterns consistent with workload.

Attached: audit-query-results-20260709.csv (summary) and raw-logs-sample-07-07.tar.gz (redacted sample).

We will continue deeper correlation (IDS logs, VPC flow logs, and external partner egress lists). No indicators of data exfiltration have been found so far.

—Monica
Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

(Attachments: audit-query-results-20260709.csv, raw-logs-sample-07-07.tar.gz)

From: Alex Gomez <security@fintegrity.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Tara Singh <compliance@fintegrity.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous outbound connections 07/07 — follow-up questions

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple of follow-ups:
1) Can you enumerate the specific log sources and exact time ranges you pulled for the statement “no indicators of data exfiltration”? Our auditors will want the exact windows and hashes for the artifacts.
2) Will Redwood provide a signed attestation or letter for our procurement/compliance team stating that no Fintegrity customer data left your environment as a result of the 07/07 spikes?

If you can provide the hashes and the log object names we can close our incident ticket quickly.

Thanks,
Alex

---
Tara Singh (cc) — Fintegrity compliance lead — would you prefer a formal letter or the technical artifact bundle?

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <security@fintegrity.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Tara Singh <compliance@fintegrity.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous outbound connections 07/07 — final audit summary and artifacts

Alex / Tara — attaching the final artifact bundle and a concise technical statement. High-level summary:
- Systems checked: NAT gateway flow logs (vpc-flow), instance syslogs, inference service application logs (stdout/stderr), S3 access logs, IAM role assumption logs, and managed Redis audit logs.
- Time windows analyzed: 2026-07-07T02:30:00Z through 2026-07-07T03:30:00Z (primary window), with supporting queries over 2026-07-07T00:00:00Z–2026-07-07T06:00:00Z.
- Findings: all egress spikes correlate to internal health-check retries to an upstream monitoring probe (misconfigured endpoint) and three automated debug sessions initiated by our automated diagnostic tooling. Byte counts per event are small (<1.5MB) and content headers correspond to probe payloads — no customer payload schema detected.
- Evidence artifacts: object names and SHA256 hashes uploaded to your read-only Drive folder (link below). The artifact bundle contains query SQL, CSV summaries, and redacted raw log samples.

We cannot provide a legal attestation on behalf of Redwood; however, from a technical perspective and based on the exhaustive checks above, we observed no indicators of data exfiltration or unauthorized export of customer data for the windows reviewed. If you require an executed statement for procurement, we can route that request through our legal team (this will take additional time).

Artifact links/hashes:
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/Fintegrity/incident-20260707-audit-summary
- audit-bundle-20260712.tar.gz — SHA256: 3b2f7e8c9ea4d5f2e4a1b6c5a8e9f4f2b0c3d6a7e5f1c2b3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1

Next steps: schedule a 30-min postmortem call this week to walk through the queries and sanity checks. Markus will coordinate if you'd like to include procurement/legal.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Cc: Markus Klein — VP, Customer Reliability (markus_klein@redwood.ai)
